title: Input
intro: raven.input controls keyboard repeat and mouse acceleration. Save to apply changes.

blocks.label: Keyboard options
rows: Repeats per second, from 0 to 1000. Use 0 to disable repeat.
Delay before repeating, from 0 to 60000 milliseconds.

blocks.text: Raven sends these values to applications. An application may implement its own repeat behavior. Changing repeat settings does not release held keys or change their shortcuts.

blocks.label: Mouse acceleration profiles
rows: Use each mouse’s libinput default. This is the default setting.
Disable speed-dependent acceleration. Movement still uses libinput’s constant device scaling.

blocks.text: Applies to mice with configurable acceleration profiles, including mice connected later. Touchpads, pointing sticks, and devices without configurable profiles are left unchanged. This setting does not change pointer speed.

-- Disable mouse acceleration
raven.input { mouse = { accel_profile = "flat" } }

-- Enable mouse acceleration
raven.input { mouse = { accel_profile = "adaptive" } }

-- Restore each mouse’s default
raven.input { mouse = { accel_profile = "default" } }
Choose one profile and edit your existing raven.input block. Save to apply it; no session restart is needed.

If a connected mouse cannot use the requested profile, Raven rejects the reload before applying the other settings. If a newly connected mouse cannot use the active profile, it keeps its existing profile and Raven logs the error.
Automation tools using wlr-virtual-pointer-unstable-v1 can send mouse clicks, movement, and scrolling. Launch them with a normal spawn keybinding. This does not provide virtual keyboard input.

blocks.title: Trusted tools only
blocks.text: Any client with access to Raven’s Wayland socket can use this protocol to control the pointer. There is no separate permission prompt.
